questions.question: How does term-at-a-time scoring traverse an inverted index?
options: It consumes one query term's postings before moving to the next term
It completes one document before reading another posting
It scans every stored document in file order
It reads only documents already in the top-k heap

questions.question: What state does a basic term-at-a-time scorer use to combine contributions?
options: A phrase dictionary ordered by position
An accumulator keyed by document identifier
A heap containing one entry per vocabulary term
A table containing only query norms

questions.question: What is a key memory advantage of document-at-a-time top-k scoring?
options: It stores a dense vector for every document
It never stores posting iterators
It can finalize candidates into a size-k heap without retaining every touched score
It removes the need for document identifiers

questions.question: In conjunctive document-at-a-time retrieval, which iterator movement is useful?
options: Rewind every list after each match
Advance the longest list by exactly one posting
Decode positions before checking document identifiers
Seek lagging lists toward the greatest current document identifier

questions.question: Postings are a:(2,1.5),(5,0.7) and b:(2,0.8),(7,1.2). What score is finalized for document 2 under additive scoring?
Why should an optimized traversal be compared with an exhaustive reference scorer?
options: To ensure compressed postings are larger
To verify traversal changes do not alter intended ranking results
To force every query to use TAAT
To eliminate the need for relevance judgments

questions.question: What does a champion list normally contain for a term?
options: Every document not containing the term
Only documents with the smallest identifiers
Documents with the highest term-specific weights
All queries previously using the term

questions.question: What is the primary goal of index elimination?
options: Increase vocabulary size
Preserve word order in every posting
Compute every score twice
Reduce postings or candidates considered during ranking

questions.question: What happens when champion-list size r is made smaller?
options: Candidate cost usually falls while miss risk rises
Candidate cost and miss risk both always fall
Every exhaustive top-k result is guaranteed
Term weights cease to matter

questions.question: Why can a document outside every per-term champion list still be highly relevant?
options: It must have no query terms
Moderate evidence from several terms can combine into a strong total
Champion lists contain only deleted documents
Its document identifier changes the tf-idf formula

questions.question: A first tier returns k documents at threshold 0.15, while an omitted candidate may score 0.9. What should the ranker do?
options: Stop because the heap has k entries
Return only one result
Search the fallback tier because stopping is not justified
Lower every omitted score to zero

questions.question: Which evaluation most directly quantifies champion-list quality?
options: Average vocabulary spelling length
Number of index segments alone
Percentage of query terms removed
Recall of exhaustive top-k results at the chosen candidate budget

questions.question: What information lets WAND skip candidates safely?
options: Valid upper bounds on possible term score contributions
Random samples of document identifiers
The average query character count
A fixed champion-list size only

questions.question: What is the top-k threshold after a min-heap of k competitive results is full?
options: The greatest score in the heap
The smallest score currently in the heap
The sum of all query upper bounds
The score of the newest indexed document

questions.question: Upper bounds 0.4, 0.7, and 0.8 are accumulated against threshold 1.5. At which cumulative value can the WAND pivot be selected?
Why does pruning usually strengthen after good results have been found?
options: Posting lists become unsorted
Term upper bounds become negative
The query gains new terms
The heap threshold rises

questions.question: What is the correctness consequence of underestimating a term upper bound?
options: A true top-k document may be skipped
More harmless candidates are fully scored
The top-k heap becomes larger than k
Every document receives the same score

questions.question: Why can block-level maximum scores outperform one global maximum per term?
options: They make posting lists unsorted
They provide tighter local bounds that permit more skipping
They remove all bound metadata
They guarantee filters accept every candidate
